## Setup

```{r setup, include=FALSE}
knitr::opts_chunk$set(echo = TRUE)
```

## Description

Primary source:

<https://ngs101.com/how-to-analyze-single-cell-rna-seq-data-complete-beginners-guide-part-4-cell-type-identification/>

**Dataset reminder**: GSE174609 is a periodontitis study (8 samples: 4
Healthy + 4 Post-Treatment PBMC samples). Peripheral blood is an ideal
dataset for learning annotation because it has well-characterized cell
types, clear canonical markers, and mature reference atlases.

Walkthrough 3 produced an integrated, batch-corrected, and clustered Seurat
object. Clustering only groups transcriptionally similar cells together -
it says nothing about *what those cells are*. This walkthrough converts
"Cluster 0, 1, 2 ..." into biologically meaningful labels such as "CD4+ T
cells" or "Classical Monocytes."

There is no single correct way to do this, so the original tutorial (and
this walkthrough) uses **four complementary approaches** and then manually
reconciles the results into a consensus:

1. **Manual annotation** - canonical marker genes plus data-driven marker
   discovery (`FindAllMarkers`). Time-consuming but the closest thing to a
   gold standard, because it incorporates biological reasoning that no
   algorithm currently replicates.
2. **SingleR** - reference-based annotation. Correlates each cell's
   expression profile against a curated, pre-labeled reference atlas
   (`celldex`) and transfers the best-matching label.
3. **scType** - marker-based gene set scoring. Uses a curated database of
   positive/negative marker genes per cell type and scores each cluster's
   enrichment.
4. **scCATCH** - tissue-specific automated annotation. Automatically finds
   cluster marker genes and matches them against a tissue-specific reference
   database (`cellmatch`).

Different methods fail in different ways, so agreement across methods builds
confidence, and disagreement flags clusters that need closer inspection.

**This .Rmd is part 1 of 3**. Clusters from walkthrough 3 are given biological
identities by inspecting canonical marker genes and data-driven cluster
markers, then assigning a manual label to each cluster. Parts 2 and 3 add
automated annotation (SingleR, scType, scCATCH) and compare the methods.

Code is taken from the source article's code blocks (steps 1-8). Changes made
for this notebook series: hard-coded values moved into the YAML front matter,
paths built from `params` rather than `setwd()`, and changes marked `ADDED:` or
`FIX:` in comments.

## Libraries and directories

```{r step1_libs_data}
library(here)

# Core single-cell analysis
library(Seurat)
library(SeuratObject)

# Visualization and data manipulation
library(ggplot2)
library(dplyr)
library(patchwork)
library(scales)
library(viridis)

source(here::here("helper_functions", "params_read.R"))
params <- params_ingest()

# Set working directory
base.dir <- params$base.dir
integr.dir <- file.path(base.dir, params$integr.dir)
annot.dir <- file.path(integr.dir, params$annot.subdir)

# Create output directories
for (d in c("plots", "plots/manual_annotation", "annotations")) {
  if (!dir.exists(file.path(annot.dir, d))) dir.create(file.path(annot.dir, d), recursive = TRUE)
}

# Set random seed for reproducibility
set.seed(params$seed)

# Configure plotting defaults
theme_set(theme_classic(base_size = 12))

# Column names and colors from params
cluster.col <- params$cluster.col
sample.col <- params$sample.col
condition.col <- params$condition.col
condition.colors <- setNames(unlist(params$condition.palette), unlist(params$condition.levels))

# Intermediate file to be passed on to part 2
annotated_part1.file <- "merged_integrated_clustered_manual_annotated.rds"
```

## Load integrated data from tutorial 3

```{r step2_load_obj}
# Path to integrated Seurat object from tutorial 3
integrated_path <- file.path(integr.dir, params$integrated.rds)

# Load the object
cat("Reading in integrated Seurat object:", integrated_path, "\n")
integrated_seurat <- readRDS(integrated_path)

stopifnot(cluster.col %in% colnames(integrated_seurat@meta.data))

# Determine which UMAP to use (from best integration method in Part 3)
available_reductions <- names(integrated_seurat@reductions)
umap_reduction <- intersect(unlist(params$umap.priority), available_reductions)[1]
if (is.na(umap_reduction)) stop("None of params$umap.priority found in object reductions: ",
                                paste(available_reductions, collapse = ", "))
cat("Assays:", paste(names(integrated_seurat@assays), collapse = ", "), "\n")
cat("Reductions:", paste(available_reductions, collapse = ", "), "\n")
cat("Using UMAP reduction:", umap_reduction, "\n")
```

### Visualize the starting point

```{r step3_start_plots, fig.width = 14, fig.height = 10}
# Create multi-panel overview
p1 <- DimPlot(integrated_seurat, reduction = umap_reduction,
              group.by = cluster.col, label = TRUE, label.size = 5,
              pt.size = 0.1,
              shuffle = TRUE) +
  ggtitle("Clusters (Pre-Annotation)") +
  theme(plot.title = element_text(face = "bold", size = 14))

p2 <- DimPlot(integrated_seurat, reduction = umap_reduction,
              group.by = sample.col, pt.size = 0.1,
              shuffle = TRUE) +
  ggtitle("Samples") +
  theme(legend.text = element_text(size = 7))

p3 <- DimPlot(integrated_seurat, reduction = umap_reduction,
              group.by = condition.col, pt.size = 0.1,
              shuffle = TRUE) +
  ggtitle("Condition") +
  scale_color_manual(values = condition.colors)

# Combine
p_overview <- (p1 | p2) / (p3 | plot_spacer())
print(p_overview)

ggsave(file.path(annot.dir, "plots/00_starting_clusters.png"), p_overview,
       width = 14, height = 10, dpi = params$plot.dpi)
```

## Normalize and scale data

This section may not be necesary if the integrated object already has a normalized RNA assay. However, it is included here to ensure that the RNA assay is normalized and scaled for marker analysis and heatmap plotting.
Set to `eval = FALSE` by default.

```{r step4_normalize, eval = FALSE}
# Tutorial 3 could leave SCT as the default assay and the RNA assay with
# per-sample layers; work on a single joined RNA assay for normalization,
# marker tests and scaling
DefaultAssay(integrated_seurat) <- "RNA"
integrated_seurat <- JoinLayers(integrated_seurat)
Idents(integrated_seurat) <- cluster.col

# Normalize data (log-normalization)
integrated_seurat <- NormalizeData(integrated_seurat,
                                   normalization.method = "LogNormalize",
                                   scale.factor = params$norm.scale.factor,
                                   verbose = FALSE)

# Scale all genes (required for DoHeatmap and marker analysis)
integrated_seurat <- ScaleData(integrated_seurat,
                               features = rownames(integrated_seurat),
                               verbose = FALSE)
```

### A caveat: `return.only.var.genes` and missing canonical markers with `SCTransform`

If preceding work has used normalization with an `SCTransform` call and
`return.only.var.genes = TRUE` (the default), only genes selected as highly
variable will have corrected values in the `data` and `scale.data` layers
of the `SCT` assay. Canonical marker genes used for manual annotation are not
guaranteed to be highly variable (e.g. broadly-expressed lineage markers can have
low cell-to-cell variance), so some may be missing from these layers and would
silently fail to plot with `VlnPlot`/`FeaturePlot`/`DotPlot`/`DoHeatmap`.

`Seurat::GetResidual()` computes corrected values for specific genes on
demand, regardless of whether they were originally flagged as variable.
Run this before checking marker presence below.

## Manual annotation: canonical marker genes

### Understanding PBMC cell types

Approximate expected composition of a healthy human PBMC sample (varies
with disease, age, and technical factors):

| Cell Type | Expected % | Key Markers | Function |
|---|---|---|---|
| T cells | 50-70% | CD3D, CD3E, CD3G | Adaptive immunity |
| &nbsp;&nbsp;CD4+ T cells | 30-40% | CD3+, CD4+, IL7R | Helper T cells |
| &nbsp;&nbsp;CD8+ T cells | 20-30% | CD3+, CD8A, CD8B | Cytotoxic T cells |
| B cells | 10-15% | CD79A, MS4A1 (CD20), CD19 | Antibody production |
| NK cells | 5-10% | NKG7, GNLY, NCAM1 (CD56) | Innate cytotoxicity |
| Monocytes | 10-20% | CD14, LYZ, S100A8, S100A9 | Phagocytosis |
| &nbsp;&nbsp;Classical | ~80% of mono | CD14+, FCGR3A- (CD16-) | CD14+ monocytes |
| &nbsp;&nbsp;Non-classical | ~20% of mono | CD14low, FCGR3A+ (CD16+) | CD16+ monocytes |
| Dendritic cells | 1-2% | FCER1A, CST3 | Antigen presentation |
| Plasmacytoid DC | <1% | IL3RA, GZMB, SERPINF1 | Type I interferon |
| Platelets | Variable | PPBP, PF4, GP9 | Usually contamination |

```{r step5_canonical_markers}

# Define comprehensive marker panel for PBMC cell types
canonical_markers <- list(
  "T_cells" = c("CD3D", "CD3E", "CD3G"),
  "CD4_T" = c("CD3D", "CD4", "IL7R"),
  "CD8_T" = c("CD3D", "CD8A", "CD8B"),
  "B_cells" = c("CD79A", "MS4A1", "CD19"),
  "NK_cells" = c("NKG7", "GNLY", "NCAM1"),
  "Monocytes" = c("CD14", "LYZ", "S100A8", "S100A9"),
  "Classical_Mono" = c("CD14", "S100A8", "FCGR3A"),
  "Non_Classical_Mono" = c("FCGR3A", "MS4A7"),
  "Dendritic_cells" = c("FCER1A", "CST3"),
  "Plasmacytoid_DC" = c("IL3RA", "GZMB", "SERPINF1"),
  "Platelets" = c("PPBP", "PF4", "GP9")
)

# Check which markers are present in dataset
all_genes <- rownames(integrated_seurat)

for (cell_type in names(canonical_markers)) {
  markers <- canonical_markers[[cell_type]]
  present <- markers %in% all_genes

  cat(sprintf("%-20s: %d/%d markers present\n",
              cell_type, sum(present), length(markers)))

  if (!all(present)) {
    missing <- markers[!present]
    cat(sprintf("  Missing: %s\n", paste(missing, collapse = ", ")))
  }
}

# Platelets: Missing GP9
```

### Visualize canonical markers

Violin and UMAP feature plots are saved to `plots/manual_annotation/`; the
combined dot plot is also shown below.

```{r step6_visualize_markers, fig.width = 12, fig.height = 10}

# Function to create violin plots for a marker set
plot_violin_markers <- function(markers, cell_type_name, filename_suffix) {
  present_markers <- markers[markers %in% rownames(integrated_seurat)]

  if (length(present_markers) == 0) {
    cat("  ⚠ No markers present for", cell_type_name, "\n")
    return(NULL)
  }

  cat("  •", cell_type_name, ":", length(present_markers), "markers\n")

  p <- VlnPlot(integrated_seurat,
               features = present_markers,
               group.by = cluster.col,
               pt.size = 0,
               ncol = 3) &
    theme(legend.position = "none",
          axis.text.x = element_text(angle = 0, hjust = 0.5, size = 8),
          axis.title.x = element_blank(),
          plot.title = element_text(size = 11, face = "bold"))

  n_rows <- ceiling(length(present_markers) / 3)
  height <- max(4, n_rows * 2.5)

  ggsave(file.path(annot.dir, paste0("plots/manual_annotation/violin_", filename_suffix, ".png")),
         p, width = 14, height = height, dpi = params$plot.dpi)

  return(p)
}

# Function to create UMAP feature plots for a marker set
plot_umap_markers <- function(markers, cell_type_name, filename_suffix) {
  present_markers <- markers[markers %in% rownames(integrated_seurat)]

  if (length(present_markers) == 0) {
    return(NULL)
  }

  p <- FeaturePlot(integrated_seurat,
                   features = present_markers,
                   reduction = umap_reduction,
                   ncol = 4,
                   pt.size = 0.1) &
    theme(plot.title = element_text(size = 10),
          axis.text = element_blank(),
          axis.ticks = element_blank(),
          legend.position = "right")

  n_rows <- ceiling(length(present_markers) / 4)
  height <- max(4, n_rows * 3)

  ggsave(file.path(annot.dir, paste0("plots/manual_annotation/umap_", filename_suffix, ".png")),
         p, width = 16, height = height, dpi = params$plot.dpi)

  return(p)
}

# Generate plots for ALL cell types
for (cell_type_key in names(canonical_markers)) {
  markers <- canonical_markers[[cell_type_key]]
  cell_type_name <- gsub("_", " ", cell_type_key)

  plot_violin_markers(markers, cell_type_name, cell_type_key)
  plot_umap_markers(markers, cell_type_name, cell_type_key)
}

# Create comprehensive DotPlot showing all key markers
all_markers <- unique(unlist(canonical_markers))
all_markers_present <- all_markers[all_markers %in% rownames(integrated_seurat)]

p_dotplot <- DotPlot(integrated_seurat,
                     features = all_markers_present,
                     group.by = cluster.col,
                     cols = c("white", "firebrick")) +
  coord_flip() +
  theme(axis.text.x = element_text(angle = 45, hjust = 1, size = 9),
        axis.text.y = element_text(size = 8)) +
  labs(title = "All Canonical Markers by Cluster",
       subtitle = paste(length(all_markers_present), "markers across all PBMC cell types"))
print(p_dotplot)

ggsave(file.path(annot.dir, "plots/manual_annotation/dotplot_all_canonical_markers.png"), p_dotplot,
       width = 12, height = max(8, length(all_markers_present) * 0.15), dpi = params$plot.dpi)
```

## Manual annotation: data-driven marker discovery

Since `integrated_seurat_integrated` could have been created by running
`SCTransform` across multiple sample layers (walkthrough 3, part 1; in `dev`
subfolder 2026-10-25), the `SCT` assay may hold separate correction models
per sample. `PrepSCTFindMarkers()` re-corrects counts to a common sequencing
depth so that differential expression p-values and fold-changes are comparable
across samples - this step is required before `FindAllMarkers` on an `SCT` assay
and is *not* part of the standard-`NormalizeData` workflow.

```{r step7_findallmarkers, fig.width = 12, fig.height = 14}

# Gene patterns removed from marker lists, species-dependent
# (article: "^RP[SL]" and "^MT-", human)
if (params$species == "human") {
  ribo.regex <- "^RP[SL]"; mito.regex <- "^MT-"
} else if (params$species == "mouse") {
  ribo.regex <- "^Rp[sl]"; mito.regex <- "^mt-"
} else {
  stop("params$species must be 'human' or 'mouse'")
}

# Find markers for each cluster vs all other cells
cluster_markers <- FindAllMarkers(
  integrated_seurat,
  only.pos = TRUE,
  min.pct = params$markers.min_pct,
  logfc.threshold = params$markers.logfc,
  verbose = FALSE
)

# Remove ribosomal and mitochondrial genes
cluster_markers_filtered <- cluster_markers %>%
  filter(!grepl(ribo.regex, gene)) %>%
  filter(!grepl(mito.regex, gene))

# Get top markers per cluster
top_markers <- cluster_markers_filtered %>%
  group_by(cluster) %>%
  top_n(n = params$markers.top_n, wt = avg_log2FC) %>%
  arrange(cluster, desc(avg_log2FC))

cat("\nTop", params$markers.top_n, "markers per cluster:\n")
print(top_markers %>% select(cluster, gene, avg_log2FC, pct.1, pct.2), n = Inf)

# Save all markers
write.csv(cluster_markers_filtered,
          file.path(annot.dir, "annotations/cluster_markers_all.csv"),
          row.names = FALSE)

write.csv(top_markers,
          file.path(annot.dir, "annotations/top5_markers_per_cluster.csv"),
          row.names = FALSE)

# Create heatmap of top markers
top_genes <- top_markers$gene

p_heatmap <- DoHeatmap(
  integrated_seurat,
  features = top_genes,
  group.by = cluster.col,
  size = 3
) +
  theme(axis.text.y = element_text(size = 6)) +
  labs(title = paste("Top", params$markers.top_n, "Markers per Cluster"))
print(p_heatmap)

ggsave(file.path(annot.dir, "plots/manual_annotation/06_heatmap_top_markers.png"), p_heatmap,
       width = 12, height = 14, dpi = params$plot.dpi)
```

Interpreting the `FindAllMarkers` output: `avg_log2FC` is higher when a gene
is more specific to that cluster; `pct.1` is the percentage of cells *in*
the cluster expressing the gene; `pct.2` is the percentage of cells *outside*
the cluster expressing it. A good marker has high `pct.1`, low `pct.2`, and
a large positive `avg_log2FC`. `min.pct = 0.25` requires the gene be
detected in at least 25% of cells in the cluster before being tested at all.

## Manual annotation: assign cluster identities

**The mapping below is the source article's example for GSE174609 and must be
checked against the dot plot, violin plots and marker tables above for any new
run (different clustering resolution = different cluster numbers).**

```{r step8_manual_mapping, fig.width = 10, fig.height = 8}

# EXAMPLE MAPPING - CUSTOMIZE FOR YOUR DATA
# customized 2026-10-25
cluster_to_celltype <- c(
  "0" = "CD4+ T cells",
  "1" = "CD4+ T cells",
  "2" = "NK cells",
  "3" = "NK cells",
  "4" = "CD4+ T cells",
  "5" = "NK cells",
  "6" = "Classical Mono",
  "7" = "CD4+ T cells",
  "8" = "B cells",
  "9" = "B cells",
  "10" = "CD8+ T cells",
  "11" = "NK cells",
  "12" = "Monocytes",
  "13" = "Nonclassical Mono",
  "14" = "NK cells",
  "15" = "NK cells",
  "16" = "Platelets"
)

# Apply to all cells
cluster_ids <- as.character(integrated_seurat@meta.data[[cluster.col]])
missing_clusters <- setdiff(unique(cluster_ids), names(cluster_to_celltype)) # ADDED: check
if (length(missing_clusters) > 0) {
  warning("Clusters without a manual label: ", paste(missing_clusters, collapse = ", "))
}
integrated_seurat$manual_annotation <- unname(cluster_to_celltype[cluster_ids])

# Visualize manual annotation
p_manual <- DimPlot(
  integrated_seurat,
  reduction = umap_reduction,
  group.by = "manual_annotation",
  label = TRUE,
  label.size = 4,
  pt.size = 0.1,
  repel = TRUE
) +
  ggtitle("Manual Cell Type Annotation") +
  theme(plot.title = element_text(face = "bold", size = 14))
print(p_manual)

ggsave(file.path(annot.dir, "plots/manual_annotation/07_manual_annotation_umap.png"), p_manual,
       width = 10, height = 8, dpi = params$plot.dpi)

# Split by condition
p_manual_split <- DimPlot(
  integrated_seurat,
  reduction = umap_reduction,
  group.by = "manual_annotation",
  split.by = condition.col,
  pt.size = 0.1,
  ncol = 2
) +
  ggtitle("Manual Annotation by Condition")
print(p_manual_split)

ggsave(file.path(annot.dir, "plots/manual_annotation/08_manual_annotation_by_condition.png"),
       p_manual_split, width = 14, height = 6, dpi = params$plot.dpi)
```
